dtn.note: High-level contact-planning simulation: data waits in a queue during gaps and is sent at the configured rate during open contacts. Not a DTN (Bundle Protocol) or LunaNet implementation; no protocol overhead, acknowledgement, light time, handover or ground scheduling is modelled.

methods.direct: Engine analysis result (series and adaptive Earth-visibility intervals of the result's DTE rule); not recomputed
methods.terrain_blocked_row: Series grid: Earth centre above 0 deg elevation but its clearance above the terrain horizon <= 0; boundaries by linear interpolation
methods.rf: Free-space link budget at each sample's distance; RF-feasible = geometric open AND margin > 0 (margin boundaries by linear interpolation)
methods.relay: Two-body Keplerian orbit (GM from gm_de440.tpc); J2000 states; SPICE pxform to the lunar body-fixed frame; leg 1 vs the site's terrain horizon and the lunar sphere; leg 2 vs the lunar sphere (+ grazing altitude)
methods.timelines: Three-valued (open, closed, unknown); unknown is never counted as open or closed

limitations: A geometrically visible Earth or relay does not guarantee a working radio link.
Free-space link budget only: no atmosphere, rain, polarisation, multipath, diffraction or lunar-surface propagation effects (see NASA Glenn's Lunar Surface Propagation research).
Every RF parameter is user-entered; LUNA-OPS supplies no hardware values and no default.
The Earth endpoint is the Earth's centre; ground stations, DSN availability and scheduling are not modelled.
The relay is hypothetical and propagated as a two-body Keplerian orbit; gravity-field harmonics and third-body perturbations are neglected, so real orbits with the same elements diverge.
Relay windows come from sampling at the stated step; contacts shorter than one step can be missed.
The store-and-forward planner is a high-level contact-planning simulation, not DTN or LunaNet.
